problem_domains.problem: QML security vulnerabilities
problem_domains.description: The paper investigates inherent security weaknesses in quantum machine learning systems, including novel vulnerabilities not present in classical platforms.
problem_domains.quote: The paper conducts a systematic literature investigation to understand the fundamental association between QML security elements and aspects. Multiple security assessments of QML models receive evaluation in this review by exploring both quantum architectural weaknesses followed by surveys of suggested security measures. Our analysis introduces security vulnerabilities that do not exist in conventional platforms.
problem_domains.location: Abstract (Page 463)

problem_domains.problem: Security of QML models in practical applications (including cloud/co-tenancy settings)
problem_domains.description: The work addresses how to secure QML models as they are deployed in real-world, multi-tenant and cloud-like environments where adversaries may exploit shared hardware and noise.
problem_domains.quote: Further analysis will be crucial since it provides fundamental protection for QML systems as they are implemented across practical applications.
problem_domains.location: Abstract (Page 463)

problem_domains.problem: Quantum Trojan attacks on QNN feature maps
problem_domains.description: The paper highlights the risk of Quantum Trojan viruses that exploit feature-map encoding in quantum neural networks as a backdoor entry point.
problem_domains.quote: The QNN framework faces a security hazard because Quantum Trojan viruses operate as system entry points through archived access points. The system enables speciﬁc gate activation through which perturbations can affect encoding feature map information [30, 31].
problem_domains.location: Section 4, “Feature Map for Quantum Encoding Targeting the Quantum Trojan Virus” (Page 470)

problem_domains.problem: Adversarial exploitation of quantum hardware noise
problem_domains.description: The paper treats hardware noise not only as a reliability issue but as an attack surface that adversaries can manipulate to degrade or subvert QML computations.
problem_domains.quote: Within quantum computing the accepted assumption about noise disturbances differs from traditional computing since noise serves as both a useful tool and an adversary to achieve computational results.
problem_domains.location: Section 2, “Quantum Computing Hardware Noise” (Page 468)

problem_domains.problem: Co-tenancy attacks on shared quantum hardware
problem_domains.description: The paper discusses attacks in multi-tenant quantum environments where concurrent users can induce hardware-dependent errors to disrupt or deny service.
problem_domains.quote: Multiple users running quantum programs concurrently in co-tenancy create opportunities for attackers to generate hardware-dependent errors. Quantum algorithms can experience performance decline or attackers might execute denial-of-service attacks because of such errors.
problem_domains.location: Section 4, “Making Use of Quantum Noise – Attacks via Co-Tenancy Setting” (Page 470)

problem_domains.problem: Cross-talk and shuttle-operation based attacks
problem_domains.description: The work identifies vulnerabilities where attackers exploit cross-talk and shuttle operations in superconducting and ion-trap systems to reduce reliability and leak information.
problem_domains.quote: Attackers in superconducting and ion-trap systems cause cross-talk between quantum circuits and repeated shuttle operations on shared qubits to reduce the reliability of quantum circuits. Read-out error correlations let attackers conduct information leakages.
problem_domains.location: Section 4, “Cross-Talk and Shuttle Operations” (Page 470)

problem_domains.problem: Scaling-induced adversarial sensitivity in high-dimensional quantum classifiers
problem_domains.description: The paper notes that as quantum models scale to higher dimensions, their classifiers become highly sensitive to small perturbations, increasing vulnerability to adversarial examples.
problem_domains.quote: As dimension increases in quantum systems the veriﬁcation systems need more resources to conﬁrm classiﬁcation decisions because of heightened classiﬁer sensitivity to nearby changes.
problem_domains.location: Section 4, “Scaling Pitfall – Increased Sensitivity” (Page 471)

problem_domains.problem: Exponential resource demand for robustness verification
problem_domains.description: The work frames the challenge that verifying robustness of high-dimensional quantum classifiers may require exponentially growing resources, undermining practical security guarantees.
problem_domains.quote: Quantum advantages can be negated by veriﬁcation sensitivity which needs escalating resources to grow at an exponential rate [ 32–36].
problem_domains.location: Section 4, “Scaling Pitfall – Exponential Resource Demand” (Page 471)

problem_domains.problem: Universal adversarial perturbations for quantum classifiers
problem_domains.description: The paper points out that small perturbations in high-dimensional spaces can threaten entire families of quantum classifiers via universal adversarial perturbations.
problem_domains.quote: A small perturbation in higher dimensions creates moderate risks for the entire set of quantum classiﬁers.
problem_domains.location: Section 4, “Universal Adversarial Perturbations” (Page 471)

problem_domains.problem: Data privacy and gradient inversion attacks in QML (including federated settings)
problem_domains.description: The review addresses privacy risks such as gradient inversion attacks against QML models, especially in federated learning scenarios.
problem_domains.quote: The researchers of Kumar et al. [52] studied QML models with excessive parameters and expressive encoding which naturally block gradient inversion attacks. The analyzed model structures operating under federated learning conditions presented serious obstacles to attackers who wished to develop attacks.
problem_domains.location: Section 4, “Inherent Privacy” (Page 472)

problem_domains.problem: Need for systematic understanding of QML security landscape
problem_domains.description: The paper positions itself as addressing a gap in systematically mapping vulnerabilities, attacks, and defenses in QML security.
problem_domains.quote: The surve y examines QML security features to reveal the built-in system security weaknesses and defensive strategies of advanced QML systems.
problem_domains.location: Introduction (Page 464)

solution_approaches.approach: quantum communication networks (QCNs)
solution_approaches.description: The chapter proposes quantum communication networks, based on quantum mechanics, as a way to achieve unbreakable encryption and fast information transfer.
solution_approaches.quote: Quantum communication networks (QCNs) are a game-changer for secure and fast information transfer by using the principles of quantum mechanics to achieve unbreakable encryption and incredibly speedy data transmission.
solution_approaches.location: Abstract, Page 18

solution_approaches.approach: quantum key distribution (QKD)
solution_approaches.description: QKD is presented as a secure communication technique that generates and distributes encryption keys using qubit properties and entanglement to detect eavesdropping.
solution_approaches.quote: QKD is a secure communication technique that generates and distributes encryption keys based on quantum physics. In order to ensure that any effort at eavesdropping can be identiﬁed, QKD makes use of qubit characteristics and entanglement, offering a high degree of security for cryptographic private information.
solution_approaches.location: Section 2.3 Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), Page 20

solution_approaches.approach: use of superposition and entanglement for secure communication
solution_approaches.description: The chapter describes leveraging superposition and entanglement to detect eavesdropping and enable secure protocols like QKD and teleportation.
solution_approaches.quote: Quantum communication networks address the vulnerabilities of classical communication by applying the principles of quantum mechanics to ensure safe data transmission. The fundamental advantage of quantum communication lies in its ability to detect any eavesdropping attempt, a feature that classical systems lack. This is achieved through the phenomena of superposition and entanglement, which are fundamental to quantum mechanics.
solution_approaches.location: Introduction, Page 19

solution_approaches.approach: no-cloning theorem as a security mechanism
solution_approaches.description: The no-cloning theorem is used as a foundational security property preventing undetectable copying of quantum states in QKD.
solution_approaches.quote: The no-cloning theorem ensures that an eaves-dropper cannot make perfect copies of qubits in a QKD protocol, thereby preventing undetectable interception of the key.
solution_approaches.location: Section 2.5 No-Cloning Theorem, Page 22

solution_approaches.approach: quantum repeaters with entanglement swapping and quantum error correction
solution_approaches.description: Quantum repeaters use entanglement swapping, quantum error correction codes, and heralded entanglement generation to extend secure quantum communication over long distances.
solution_approaches.quote: Instead, quantum repeaters use advanced methods such as entanglement swapping and quantum error correction to overcome loss and decoherence, ensuring the integrity of quantum information over extended distances [46].
solution_approaches.location: Section 3.1 Quantum Repeaters, Page 24

solution_approaches.approach: heralded entanglement generation
solution_approaches.description: Heralded entanglement generation is proposed to ensure successful entanglement between distant nodes before communication proceeds.
solution_approaches.quote: Heralded entanglement generation is a technique used to ensure that entanglement is successfully established between distant nodes before proceeding with communication.
solution_approaches.location: Section 3.1 Quantum Repeaters, Page 24

solution_approaches.approach: quantum memory (atomic ensembles, optical cavities, solid-state systems)
solution_approaches.description: Quantum memory technologies such as atomic ensembles, optical cavities, and solid-state systems are proposed to store and synchronize quantum information in networks.
solution_approaches.quote: Quantum memory is a crucial component for the advancement and practical implementation of quantum communication networks. It serves as a storage medium for quantum information, enabling the synchronization, buffering, and long-term preservation of quantum states.
solution_approaches.location: Section 3.3 Quantum Memory, Page 26

solution_approaches.approach: quantum processors (superconducting qubits, trapped ions, photonic qubits)
solution_approaches.description: Quantum processors based on superconducting qubits, trapped ions, and photonic qubits are described as engines to execute quantum algorithms and protocols within quantum communication networks.
solution_approaches.quote: Quantum processors are the computational engines that enable the execution of quantum algorithms and protocols within quantum communication networks. These processors manipulate quantum bits (qubits) according to the principles of quantum mechanics, offering capabilities that surpass those of classical processors for certain tasks [ 8].
solution_approaches.location: Section 3.4 Quantum Processors, Page 27–28

solution_approaches.approach: quantum error correction codes and fault-tolerant architectures
solution_approaches.description: Quantum error correction codes and fault-tolerant quantum computing techniques are proposed to protect qubits from errors in communication networks.
solution_approaches.quote:
Quantum processors implement error correction techniques to protect qubits from decoherence and errors introduced during computation.
(i) Quantum Error Correction Codes (QECC): Logical qubits are encoded into entangled states of multiple physical qubits via QECCs.
solution_approaches.location: Section 3.4.2 Error Correction and Fault Tolerance, Page 29

solution_approaches.approach: quantum cryptography
solution_approaches.description: Quantum cryptography is proposed as a physical application of quantum computing to enhance 5G security.
solution_approaches.quote: The chapter also investigates the physical applications of quantum computing such as quantum cryptography network resource optimiza- tion and enhanced signal processing.
solution_approaches.location: Abstract (Page 46)

solution_approaches.approach: quantum algorithms for improving the overall efficiency of the 5G network
solution_approaches.description: The chapter explores implementing quantum algorithms to improve 5G network efficiency.
solution_approaches.quote: The issues like implementation of quantum algorithms for improving the overall efﬁciency of the 5G network and its integra- tion with other future technologies have also been explored in the context of the deployment of 6G networks.
solution_approaches.location: Abstract (Page 46)

solution_approaches.approach: quantum algorithms for optimizing network management and traffic flow
solution_approaches.description: Quantum algorithms are proposed to solve complex optimization problems in 5G network management and traffic flow.
solution_approaches.quote: The complex optimization problem of 5G networks can be resolved by using quantum computing techniques. For example, quantum algorithms can be developed to tackle real-time network trafﬁc, load balancing of the network, efﬁcient resources and locations to the calls, and to manage high network performance.
solution_approaches.location: Section 1.4 Synergy Between Quantum Computing and 5G (Page 51)

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum Key Distribution (quantum computing key distribution) for 5G security
solution_approaches.description: Quantum key distribution is proposed as an encryption method to protect data over 5G networks.
solution_approaches.quote: V arious encryption algorithms in the form of a quantum computing key distribution could be used for data protec- tion while transferring or transmitting over 5G networks.
solution_approaches.location: Section 1.4 Synergy Between Quantum Computing and 5G (Page 51)

solution_approaches.approach: quantum networking / quantum internet integrated with 5G

solution_approaches.quote: In the future, quantum networking will the integrated into the 5G netw- orks to create highly secure quantum Internet to support high bandwidth applications and low latency communication over it.
solution_approaches.location: Section 1.4 Synergy Between Quantum Computing and 5G (Page 51)

solution_approaches.approach: Shor’s Algorithm
solution_approaches.description: Quantum integer factorization algorithm used to break classical encryption like RSA and motivate quantum-safe encryption in 5G.
solution_approaches.quote:
Shor’s Algorithm: This algorithm is designed for integer factorization in classical 
encryption techniques 
like RSA. In context to the 5G network, the algorithm 
split the conventional cryptographic protocols to satisfy the need for quantum 
encryption in the future and form the basis of secure communication in quantum-
enabled networks.
solution_approaches.location: Section 2.3 Quantum Algorithms Relevant to Networking, Page 52

solution_approaches.approach: Grover’s Algorithm
solution_approaches.description: Quantum search algorithm proposed for optimizing network routing and load balancing.
solution_approaches.quote:
Grover’s Algorithm: This algorithm is particularly useful to increase the speed 
of searching 
operations onto the unsorted data... it could be utilized for the optimization of network routing to 
ﬁnd the most efﬁcient communication path within the large network. It could 
also be beneﬁcial in load balancing by efﬁciently searching various possible 
conﬁgurations.
solution_approaches.location: Section 2.3 Quantum Algorithms Relevant to Networking, Page 52–53

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD)
solution_approaches.description: Quantum cryptographic protocol to exchange cryptographic keys and create highly secure communication channels.
solution_approaches.quote:
Quantum Key Distribution (QKD): Considering network security as a paramount 
concern in 
next-generation 5G6G networks, protocols like quantum key distribu-
tion exploit quantum mechanics principles to exchange the cryptographic keys 
between two communication parties. These protocols are of great importance 
to create highly secure communication channels such that the data transmission 
over time may not be intercepted or tempered by a third party.
solution_approaches.location: Section 2.3 Quantum Algorithms Relevant to Networking, Page 53

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum Walks
solution_approaches.description: Quantum walk algorithms used to resolve search problems and optimize network routes to increase data transmission rate.
solution_approaches.quote:
Quantum Walks: Quantum lock algorithms are particularly used to resolve search 
problems and 
for route optimization of the network. They’re particularly helpful 
to increase the data transmission rate and to avoid network condition problems.
solution_approaches.location: Section 2.3 Quantum Algorithms Relevant to Networking, Page 53

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum cryptography for secure communication
solution_approaches.description: Use of quantum cryptography and QKD in 5G to detect tampering and maintain data integrity.
solution_approaches.quote:
Quantum cryptography techniques exploit the principle of quantum mechanics to 
protect the network data from inception and tampering. In context to the 5G networks, 
quantum cryptography utilizes quantum key distribution to enhance data security. 
Any attempt for the temping of data can be detected as it modiﬁes the quantum 
state of the key that indirectly reﬂects the presence of a potential eavesdropper.
solution_approaches.location: Section 4.1 Quantum Cryptography for Secure Communication, Page 58

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum-assisted signal processing
solution_approaches.description: Use of superposition and entanglement in quantum algorithms for error correction and signal optimization in 5G.
solution_approaches.quote:
Contrary to this the quantum assisted signal 
processing exploits the concept of superposition and entanglement to overcome these 
challenges... A typical application of quantum signal processing in a 5G involves 
error correction 
and signal optimization.
solution_approaches.location: Section 4.2 Quantum-Assisted Signal Processing, Page 59

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum algorithms for spectrum management (including quantum annealing)
solution_approaches.description: Quantum computing, particularly quantum annealing, to identify best frequency bands, manage congestion, and enable dynamic spectrum allocation.
solution_approaches.quote:
Quantum computing techniques can be proven 
beneﬁcial to deal with the situation by optimizing the task much faster as compared 
to the conventional approaches. Techniques like quantum annealing help in identi-
fying the best frequency bands while serving the various applications to the users 
while offering the least interference and maximizing throughput while handling the 
network congestion problem smartly.
solution_approaches.location: Section 4.4 Quantum Solutions for Spectrum Management, Page 60

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum computing for dynamic spectrum management
solution_approaches.description: Quantum algorithms for real-time spectrum allocation based on demand, usage patterns, and conditions, including anomaly detection.
solution_approaches.quote:
Quantum computing can also be helpful for dynamic spectrum management by 
allocating the 
spectrum on a real-time basis as per user demand, network resource 
usage patterns, and network conditions. Quantum algorithms help in faster decision-
making based on real-time datasets that allow the network to adapt to the network 
conditions. Moreover, these algorithms also help the detection of anomalies in the 
network and reduce the risk of spectral collisions.
solution_approaches.location: Section 4.4 Quantum Solutions for Spectrum Management, Page 60

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum machine learning for network optimization
solution_approaches.description: QML integrated with ML to process huge datasets, perform optimization, and enable dynamic resource allocation and traffic management.
solution_approaches.quote:
Quantum machine learning (QML) involves the integration of quantum computing 
with machine learning (ML) techniques to optimize the network resources efﬁ-
ciently for the 5G environments... Quantum machine learning addresses these chal-
lenges by processing huge datasets and performing optimization tasks more efﬁ-
ciently than conventional systems.
solution_approaches.location: Section 4.3 Quantum Machine Learning for Network Optimization, Page 59

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum cryptographic technique with quantum key distribution in 5G
solution_approaches.description: Integration of quantum cryptographic techniques and QKD into 5G for secure communication in heterogeneous environments.
solution_approaches.quote:
The quantum 
cryptographic technique could also be beneﬁcial to integrate with the 
5G networks for secured communication in a heterogeneous environment... The quantum crypto-
graphic technique helps the protection of sensitive information from such attacks by 
integrating the quantum key distribution method.

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum hardware accelerators in 5G networks
solution_approaches.description: Deployment of quantum processors/accelerators alongside conventional systems for resource management and error correction.
solution_approaches.quote:
The introduction of the new quantum hardware could be adopted by 
the existing infrastructure by incorporating the quantum accelerators along with the 
conventional computing systems... These quantum processors can be used by the 
5G netw
orks for efﬁcient resource management, error detection, and correction at a 
greater speed.
solution_approaches.location: Section 5.1 Quantum Hardware Adaptation for Networks, Page 61

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum cloud computing for 5G
solution_approaches.description: Use of quantum cloud resources for enhanced security, optimized network management, dynamic spectrum sharing, improved AI/ML, and latency reduction.
solution_approaches.quote:
The quantum cloud computing technology has the potential to affect the 5G appli-
cation in a various aspect of network security, and resource management.

CRYSTALS-Dilithium and NTRU. These algorithms rely on the hardness of lattice

of the 
NIST-selected quantum-safe algorithms. It utilizes the LWE problem,to enable 
efﬁcient key exchange [ 10].

solution_approaches.approach: CRYSTALS-Dilithium

withstand attacks 
from quantum computers.

solution_approaches.approach: NTRU

ke
y cryptosystem introduced by Hoffstein, Pipher, and Silverman in 1996 [ 23]. 
NTRU 
exhibits very high encryption and decryption speed due to small key sizes.

The McEliece Public Key Cryptosystem is a an example of post-quantum crypto-

cheme based on error-correcting codes [ 5, 31].

bution capabilities particularly through quantum key distribution (QKD).

raphy and Quantum Cryptography.

Algorithms selected 
by NIST 
are proposed to be part of future security standards.

solution_approaches.approach: Mosca’s Inequality for migration planning
solution_approaches.description: The chapter uses Mosca’s Inequality as a framework to plan migration timelines to quantum-safe cryptography.
solution_approaches.quote:
Michele Mosca, a pioneer in quantum computing and cryp-
tography, proposed a framework to evaluate the urgency of adopting quantum-safe 
cryptography in the face of emerging quantum threats [ 34]. His analysis is known 
as Mosca’
s Inequality and helps estimate the timeline for the potential breakage of 
current cryptographic systems.
solution_approaches.location: Section 3 Timeline to Migrate to Quantum Safe Ecosystems, Page 192

solution_approaches.approach: Hash-based cryptography
solution_approaches.description: Hash-based cryptographic systems use the hardness of cryptographic hash functions to build quantum-resistant digital signatures.
solution_approaches.quote: Hash-based cryptographic systems like SPHINCS+ achieve quantum resistance using the security of hash functions to create secure digital signatures [ 1, 20]. Hash-based cryptography utilizes the well-studied hardness of cryptographic hash functions, making it highly resistant to both classical and quantum attacks.
solution_approaches.location: Section 5.3 Hash-Based Cryptography, Page 190–191

solution_approaches.approach: SPHINCS+
solution_approaches.description: SPHINCS+ is a stateless hash-based digital signature scheme built entirely on hash functions and designed to resist quantum attacks.
solution_approaches.quote: SPHINCS+ is a stateless, hash-based digital signature scheme speciﬁcally designed to resist quantum attacks. Unlike schemes relying on number-theoretic assumptions, SPHINCS+ is built entirely on the security of cryptographic hash functions
solution_approaches.location: Section 5.3.1 SPHINCS+, Page 191

solution_approaches.approach: WOTS+ (Winternitz One-Time Signature Plus)
solution_approaches.description: WOTS+ is a one-time signature scheme integrated into SPHINCS+ to provide secure single-use signing.
solution_approaches.quote: SPHINCS+ integrates two key One-Time Signature (OTS) schemes: Winternitz One-Time Signature Plus (WOTS+) and Full Merkle Tree-based One-Time Signature(FORS). WOTS+ offers secure, single-use signing capabilities [ 25 ]
solution_approaches.location: Section 5.3.1 SPHINCS+, Page 191

solution_approaches.approach: FORS (Full Merkle Tree-based One-Time Signature)
solution_approaches.description: FORS is an OTS scheme within SPHINCS+ that optimizes signature generation and verification.
solution_approaches.quote: FORS optimizes signature generation and veriﬁcation for better performance within the framework [ 7]. Together, these components strengthen SPHINCS+’s efﬁciency and security
solution_approaches.location: Section 5.3.1 SPHINCS+, Page 191

solution_approaches.approach: Substitution-Permutation Network (SPN)
solution_approaches.description: SPNs are symmetric-key block cipher structures, such as AES, that use alternating substitution and permutation layers for secure encryption.
solution_approaches.quote: One of the most widely used structures in symmetric ciphers is the Substitution-Permutation Network (SPN). A Substitution-Permutation Network (SPN) is a fundamental design framework used in many symmetric key block ciphers, such as the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) [ 16].
solution_approaches.location: Section 5.4 Symmetric Cryptography: Substitution-Permutation Network (SPN), Page 192

solution_approaches.approach: Picnic post-quantum digital signature scheme
solution_approaches.description: Picnic is a post-quantum digital signature algorithm that relies solely on symmetric-key primitives and zero-knowledge proofs, using the LowMC block cipher and MPC-in-the-Head.
solution_approaches.quote: Picnic is a post-quantum digital signature algorithm designed to resist quantum attacks by relying solely on symmetric-key primitives, such as block ciphers and hash functions [ 13]. It does not depend on hard mathematical problems like factoring or lattices, making it an attractive alternative in post-quantum cryptography. Picnic is based on symmetric primitives and zero-knowledge proofs. It uses the LowMC block cipher, optimized for efﬁcient implementation. Picnic is secure due to the Multi-Party Computation-in-the-Head (MPCitH) paradigm.
solution_approaches.location: Section 5.4.1 Picnic: A Symmetric Post-quantum Digital Signature Scheme, Page 193

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD)
solution_approaches.description: QKD uses quantum principles such as superposition, entanglement, and the no-cloning theorem to distribute random keys securely between two parties.
solution_approaches.quote: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) provides theoretically unbreakable security by leveraging quantum principles like superposition,entanglement and No cloning theorem [ 41, 43]. Real-world implementations of QKD, such as satellite-based networks and ﬁber-optic systems, demonstrate its practical viability and scalability [ 41]. QKD is a method for distributing random keys securely between two parties (Alice and Bob) who do not initially share any secret information.
solution_approaches.location: Section 6 Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), Page 194

solution_approaches.approach: BB84 protocol
solution_approaches.description: BB84 is a foundational QKD protocol that encodes bits in non-orthogonal polarization bases to enable eavesdropping detection.
solution_approaches.quote: The BB84 protocol, introduced by Bennett and Brassard in 1984 [ 4], is the ﬁrst and most widely studied QKD protocol. It uses quantum bits (qubits) to encode information in different bases, allowing the detection of eavesdropping through discrepancies in the measurement outcomes.
solution_approaches.location: Section 6.2.1 BB84 Protocol, Page 198

solution_approaches.approach: B92 protocol
solution_approaches.description: B92 is a simplified QKD protocol that uses only two non-orthogonal quantum states to encode binary information.
solution_approaches.quote: The B92 protocol, proposed by Bennett in 1992 [ 2], is a simpliﬁed variation of the BB84 Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocol. Unlike BB84, which uses four non-orthogonal quantum states, BB92 employs only two non-orthogonal quantum states to encode binary information, making it conceptually simpler while retaining quantum security principles.
solution_approaches.location: Section 6.2.2 B92 Protocol, Page 200

solution_approaches.approach: E91 protocol
solution_approaches.description: E91 is an entanglement-based QKD protocol that uses Bell’s inequality violations to detect eavesdropping.
solution_approaches.quote: The E91 protocol, introduced by Artur Ekert in 1991 [ 17 ], is a quantum key distribution (QKD) scheme based on quantum entanglement and Bell’s inequality. E91 utilizes quantum non-locality to detect eavesdropping.
solution_approaches.location: Section 6.2.3 E91, Page 201

solution_approaches.approach: Continuous Variable Quantum Key Distribution (CV-QKD)
solution_approaches.description: CV-QKD encodes information in Gaussian-modulated coherent states and uses homodyne or heterodyne detection compatible with telecom infrastructure.
solution_approaches.quote: Continuous Variable Quantum Key Distribution (CV -QKD) uses coherent or squeezed states of light, making it practical for implementation over existing optical ﬁber networks. It encodes information in Gaussian-modulated coherent states. It was ﬁrst proposed by Grosshans and Grangier in 2002 [ 21]. CV -QKD makes measurements using homodyne or heterodyne detection, which is compatible with standard telecom technology.
solution_approaches.location: Section 6.2.4 Continuous Variable Quantum Key Distribution (CV-QKD), Page 203

solution_approaches.approach: SARG04 protocol
solution_approaches.description: SARG04 is a BB84 variant designed to improve resistance against photon number splitting attacks by modifying encoding and key sifting.
solution_approaches.quote: The SARG04 protocol, proposed by Scarani, Acín, Ribordy, and Gisin in 2004, is a variant of the BB84 Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocol. It was designed to enhance the security of QKD systems, particularly against photon number splitting (PNS) attacks, which can exploit multi-photon pulses in weak coherent state QKD. SARG04 differs from BB84 in how the key bits are encoded and disclosed [ 46].
solution_approaches.location: Section 6.2.5 SARG04 Protocol, Page 204

solution_approaches.approach: Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution (MDI-QKD)
solution_approaches.description: MDI-QKD sends states from Alice and Bob to an untrusted third party performing Bell state measurements, removing detector side-channel vulnerabilities.
solution_approaches.quote: The proposed Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution (MDI-QKD) protocol addresses vulnerabilities in detector devices commonly exploited in quantum hacking attacks (like detector blinding attacks). It was introduced by Lo, Curty, and Qi [ 29]. MDI-QKD enhances security by making the system immune to detector-side attacks, one of the major loopholes in traditional QKD systems.
solution_approaches.location: Section 6.2.6 Measurement Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution (MDI-QKD), Page 205

solution_approaches.approach: NIST Post Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Standardization Project algorithms
solution_approaches.description: NIST-selected post-quantum algorithms such as CRYSTALS-Kyber, CRYSTALS-Dilithium, Falcon, and SPHINCS+ to replace or complement RSA and ECC.

These standardized algorithms are designed to replace or complement cryptographic systems like RSA and ECC, which are vulnerable to Shor’s algorithm on sufﬁciently powerful quantum computers.

key_claims.claim: Classical cryptographic methods are becoming defenseless to sophisticated and quantum attacks.
key_claims.quote: The rise of quantum communication is largely attributed to the increasing need for secure data transmission in an era where classical cryptographic methods are becoming defense-less to sophisticated attacks.

key_claims.claim: Quantum communication networks can ensure data remains confidential and tamper-proof even against advanced computational threats.
key_claims.quote: Quantum communication networks promise to revolutionize how we exchange information by ensuring that data remains conﬁdential and tamper-proof, even in the face of advanced computational threats posed by the advent of quantum computers [ 5].

key_claims.claim: Quantum communication can detect any eavesdropping attempt, unlike classical systems.
key_claims.quote: The fundamental advantage of quantum communication lies in its ability to detect any eavesdropping attempt, a feature that classical systems lack.

key_claims.claim: Quantum communication networks are particularly crucial for national security, financial transactions, and confidential communications.
key_claims.quote: This is particularly crucial for applications in national security, ﬁnancial transactions, and conﬁdential communications, where data integrity and privacy are paramount [ 26, 27] (Table 1).

key_claims.claim: Quantum satellites enable secure communication across vast geographical areas by extending quantum networks beyond terrestrial limitations.
key_claims.quote: These satellites extend the reach of quantum networks beyond terrestrial limitations, enabling secure communication across vast geographical areas [31].

key_claims.claim: The integration of 5G and quantum computing has great potential to improve network performance, security, and overall efficiency.
key_claims.quote: The integration of 5G and quantum computing has the great potential to impro- ve network performance security and overall efﬁciency in this chapter the feasibility of combining quantum computing with 5G technology is explored for the successful deployment of next-generation wireless communication networks.

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing can reduce the computational carbon footprint by replacing energy-intensive classical simulations and optimizations.
key_claims.quote: Data centers account for nearly 1–2% of global energy consumption [9]. Replacing intensive simulations or optimization processes with quantum-efﬁcient counterparts could have signiﬁcant energy-saving implications—making the technology itself a part of the sustainability solution.
key_claims.location: 2.5 Why Quantum Computing Matters for Sustainability, Page 75

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing is beginning to move from theoretical potential to practical deployment in industrial energy and climate applications.
key_claims.quote: These initiatives signal a shift from theoretical potential to practical deployment, reinforcing the commercial viability of quantum-based sustainability solutions.

key_claims.claim: Current quantum hardware is in the NISQ era and is not yet capable of delivering reliable results for many large-scale, real-world energy or climate problems.
key_claims.quote: Today’s quantum computers operate within the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) era, and while useful for experimentation, they are not yet capable of delivering reliable results for many large-scale, real-world problems in energy or climate applications.

key_claims.claim: Algorithmic maturity and problem-specific, fault-tolerant quantum algorithms for sustainability applications are still under development.
key_claims.quote: Many sustainability challenges, such as energy optimization or carbon material simulation, require problem-speciﬁc quantum algorithms that are both efﬁcient and fault-tolerant—an area where development is ongoing.

key_claims.claim: There is a significant shortage of interdisciplinary talent at the intersection of quantum science and sustainability domains.
key_claims.quote: There is also a signiﬁcant shortage of interdisciplinary talent capable of working at the intersection of quantum science, climate modeling, energy systems, and data science.

key_claims.claim: Access to quantum infrastructure is uneven and risks widening technological divides between developed and developing economies.
key_claims.quote: Access and equity present further barriers. Quantum computing infrastructure and cloud services are predominantly concentrated in developed economies, raising concerns about widening technological divides.

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing has dual-use potential and raises ethical and governance concerns if not properly regulated.
key_claims.quote: Like many advanced technologies, quantum computing has dual-use potential—its applications span from beneﬁcial uses in climate mitigation to sensitive domains such as surveillance and defense. Without proactive regulation and transparent design, the deployment of quantum systems in sustainability contexts could raise questions about fairness, accountability, and unintended consequences.

key_claims.claim: Hybrid quantum–classical models and quantum-inspired algorithms are already delivering tangible benefits despite hardware limitations.
key_claims.quote: However, hybrid quantum–classical models and quantum-inspired algorithms are already delivering tangible beneﬁts in operational settings.

key_claims.claim: As quantum hardware improves and collaborations expand, quantum-enhanced smart grids are expected to become practical by the late 2020s.
key_claims.quote: As quantum hardware improves and cross-disciplinary collaborations expand, these challenges are expected to diminish, making quantum-enhanced smart grids a practical reality by the late 2020s.

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing is emerging as a foundational pillar for next-generation sustainable infrastructure, not just a digital accelerator.
key_claims.quote: By addressing these themes, the chapter contributes to the emerging body of literature that positions quantum technologies not just as accelerators of digital transformation but as foundational pillars for the next generation of sustainable infrastructure.

Quantum AI models function beyond human understanding making real-time human observation extremely difﬁcult while reaching decisions at lightning speeds with extreme complexity [18]. Such systems experience catastrophic failures that include trafﬁc accidents and market crashes and security breaches faster than the ability of human operators to act [26].
key_claims.location: Section 5.2 Security Considerations – Safety of Autonomous Quantum AI Systems (Page 111–112)

key_claims.claim: Practical quantum advantage for AI, including financial applications, remains out of reach in the foreseeable future.
key_claims.quote: Research and expectation in quantum-enhanced AI development continues to thrive but practical quantum advantage remains out of reach in the foreseeable future and will need both hardware development alongside innovative algorithmic methods [59].
key_claims.location: Section 5.1 Ethical Considerations in Quantum AI – Acceleration of AI Impact (Page 106)

key_claims.claim: Quantum algorithms can dramatically accelerate big data tasks such as clustering, pattern identification, optimization, and machine learning.
key_claims.quote: Quantum mechanics principles such as superposition, entanglement, and inference enable quantum algorithms to conduct data clustering combinations at incredible speeds and with high efﬁciency for pattern identiﬁcation, optimization, and machine learning operations.

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing offers theoretical advantages over classical computing for processing large datasets via parallel evaluation of multiple possibilities.
key_claims.quote: Quantum computers have theoretical advantages when processing large data sets by simultaneously running parallel multiple possibility calculations to speed up analysis speed [7].
key_claims.location: 1.1 The Challenges of Big Data in Classical Computing, Page 123

key_claims.claim: Quantum parallelism can yield polynomial to exponential speedups for certain big data-related problems.
key_claims.quote: The speedup range from polynomial to exponential lies in two quantum algorithms which include Grover’s search algorithm and Shor’s factorization method. ... Quantum parallelism through superposition allows quantum computers to inspect a large computational domain effectively which results in substantial acceleration over classical algorithms that process speciﬁc big data-related problems.

key_claims.claim: Quantum optimization techniques provide considerable benefits for big data solutions by quickly solving difficult optimization challenges.
key_claims.quote: Quantum optimization techniques establish a considerable beneﬁt in big data solutions via their quick and efﬁcient resolution of difﬁcult optimization challenges which surpass traditional computational approaches.

key_claims.claim: Quantum machine learning can enable faster training, more advanced models, and higher accuracy than classical ML for big data.
key_claims.quote: The analysis of extensive datasets with quantum algorithms in quantum machine learning runs at higher speeds to reveal information beyond traditional methods. The analysis of big data acquires new possibilities through quantum machine learning algorithms which produce advanced model structures together with quicker training times and superior accuracy levels beyond classical machine learning approaches [18].

key_claims.claim: Hybrid approaches can already provide practical benefits by offloading computationally intensive subroutines to quantum processors while classical systems handle data and control.
key_claims.quote: Hybrid approaches allow researchers to utilize the strengths of quantum computers for speciﬁc computationally intensive tasks while relying on classical computers for data handling, control, and optimization. This division of labor makes it possible to achieve practical beneﬁts even with current quantum hardware.
key_claims.location: 4.5 Applications of Hybrid Systems in Big Data Analytics, Page 121

key_claims.claim: Current quantum hardware suffers from short qubit coherence times, limiting the complexity and length of algorithms for big data analysis.
key_claims.quote: The short coherence times of current qubits pose a signiﬁcant limitation on the complexity and length of quantum algorithms that can be executed reliably for big data analysis.

key_claims.claim: Scaling quantum computers to the size needed for large big data problems is a major engineering challenge.
key_claims.quote: Scaling quantum computers to the level necessary for solving large, complex problems inherent in big data analysis is a daunting challenge. Interconnecting a large number of qubits to create larger, more powerful systems is a very complex process [28].

key_claims.claim: High error rates and limited qubit fidelity currently undermine the reliability of quantum computations for critical big data tasks.
key_claims.quote: The high error rates and limited ﬁdelity of current quantum hardware can lead to inaccurate results, making it difﬁcult to rely on quantum computations for critical big data analysis tasks without robust error correction mechanisms in place.

key_claims.claim: Quantum error correction introduces substantial qubit overhead, which is a major challenge for scaling systems for big data.
key_claims.quote: To address the inherent noise and decoherence in quantum systems, quantum error correction (QEC) is essential. QEC involves encoding quantum information into multiple physical qubits to protect it from errors, effectively creating a more stable “logical” qubit. However, implementing QEC typically requires a substantial number of physical qubits for each logical qubit, leading to a signiﬁcant overhead in terms of qubit resources.

key_claims.claim: Combining quantum computing with machine learning can accelerate and lower the cost of drug discovery.
key_claims.quote: Thus combining ML with Quantum computing can work as a catalyst for the Drug Discovery process, ultimately lowering the drug cost.

key_claims.claim: Quantum Machine Learning can enhance diagnostic analytics, including early cancer diagnosis and predictive analytics for disease progression.
key_claims.quote: QML represents a promising ﬁeld in healthcare that enhances conventional ML models by using Quantum Computing. It utilizes QA (quantum algorithms) to examine large and intricate data more effectively. A crucial ﬁeld is diagnostic analytics in which the quantum models can swiftly identify medical data patterns like radiological images. QML can improve early cancer diagnosis by identifying subtle symptoms of the disease. Also it supports predictive analytics for improved forecasts of disease development along with patient results leading to more personalized treatments [5].

key_claims.claim: Quantum Generative Models and QGANs can better represent chemical distributions and accelerate training compared to classical models.
key_claims.quote: Suggested quantum GAN feature a hybrid generator (QGAN-HG) which can effectively learn molecular distribution to accelerate training and prevent issues in Deep Neural Networks [6]. ... Quantum Generative Models provide more beneﬁts like improved presentation of chemical distributions as compared to classical models [6].

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing can significantly accelerate drug research and initial discovery tasks, but cannot currently replace all classical functions.
key_claims.quote: QC signiﬁcantly accelerates the drug research aiding the pharmaceutical sector. No doubt QC can address complicated issues faster than the classical computers; it cannot currently substitute all classical functions.

key_claims.claim: Variational Quantum Eigensolver offers better results than conventional methods as system size increases.
key_claims.quote: Present conventional methods face the issues of precise calculations as the size of the system increases. V ariational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) offers better results.

key_claims.claim: Quantum systems are currently constrained by qubit count, noise, decoherence, and gate errors, limiting their use in complex drug discovery tasks.
key_claims.quote: Quantum computers require numerous qubits to analyze complex molecules; even then existing devices are restricted by their limited qubits count. This constraint complicated the scaling for drug discovery and the required quantum gate operations can increase error rates.
key_claims.location: Challenges Faced in the Field of Drug Discovery (Page 154-155)

key_claims.claim: There is a need for more effective and reliable quantum algorithms specifically tailored to drug discovery.
key_claims.quote: there still exists a demand for more effective and reliable algorithm for discovery of drugs. Creating such algorithms requires a thorough consideration of the domain of the problem and leveraging the advantages of QC.
key_claims.location: Challenges Faced in the Field of Drug Discovery (Page 156)

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing has great potential to transform drug discovery by speeding processes, improving candidates, and deepening understanding of molecular systems, despite current challenges.
key_claims.quote: To conclude, QC has a great prospective of transforming the process of discovery of drugs even though the certain challenges prevail. The ability to speed up drug discovery processes, improve the drug candidates and deepen the comprehension of intricate molecular systems places Quantum Computing as a thrilling frontier in Pharmaceutical Research.

key_claims.quote: Quantum Algorithms for community detection using benchmark datasets were showcased which resulted in competitive performance with traditional methods.

key_claims.quote: Quantum algorithms like the Shor’s and Grover’s pose a risk to the public key cryptography. However current quantum computing capabilities have not yet undermined the data security. V arious agencies are developing quantum cryptographic techniques with the aim of transitioning federal system by the year 2035.The major concern is that data encrypted today may be vulnerable to decryption by future quantum technologies.

key_claims.quote: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) provides theoretically unbreakable security by leveraging quantum principles like superposition,entanglement and No cloning theorem [ 41, 43]. Real-world implementations of QKD, such as satellite-based networks and ﬁber-optic systems, demonstrate its practical viability and scalability [ 41].

key_claims.claim: BB84 is a foundational protocol that has inspired more advanced QKD protocols and experimental implementations.
key_claims.quote: BB84 remains a foundational protocol in the ﬁeld of quantum cryptography and has inspired more advanced QKD protocols and experimental implementations.

key_claims.claim: B92 simplifies implementation compared to BB84 but generally has a lower key generation rate due to inconclusive measurements.
key_claims.quote: The BB92 protocol reduces the number of quantum states required, simplifying implementation while maintaining quantum security. However, it generally has a lower key generation rate compared to BB84 due to possible inconclusive measurements.

key_claims.claim: E91 provides strong theoretical security guarantees even against quantum eavesdroppers by leveraging entanglement and Bell’s inequality violation.
key_claims.quote: E91 protocol stands out because it leverages quantum entanglement and Bell’s inequality violation, providing strong theoretical security guarantees even against quantum eavesdroppers.

key_claims.claim: CV-QKD is compatible with existing telecom infrastructure and can achieve higher key rates over shorter distances without single-photon sources, but is sensitive to noise and requires precise calibration.
key_claims.quote: Compatible with existing telecom infrastructure (optical ﬁbers, standard photodetectors). Higher key rates over shorter distances. No need for single-photon sources or detectors. Sensitive to channel noise and losses. Requires precise calibration of detectors. Finite-size effects are more complex to analyze.
key_claims.location: Section 6.2.4 Continuous Variable Quantum Key Distribution (CV-QKD), Page 203–204

key_claims.claim: SARG04 offers better protection against photon number splitting attacks than BB84 by modifying the key sifting process and introducing state pairs.
key_claims.quote: By modifying the key sifting process and introducing state pairs, it provides better protection against speciﬁc attacks, such as photon number splitting (PNS) attacks.

key_claims.claim: MDI-QKD is immune to all detector side-channel attacks and can increase distance using trusted relay points, but requires precise synchronization and has reduced key rate compared to BB84.
key_claims.quote: MDI-QKD enhances security by making the system immune to detector-side attacks, one of the major loopholes in traditional QKD systems. ... However, the protocol requires precise synchronization of photons sent by Alice and Bob. Achieving this is experimentally challenging and reduces the overall key rate compared to BB84.
key_claims.location: Section 6.2.6 Measurement Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution (MDI-QKD), Page 205–206

key_claims.claim: Current cryptosystems are vulnerable to quantum attacks, motivating NIST’s PQC standardization effort.
key_claims.quote: Our current cryptosystems are vulnerable to Quantum attacks. Based on Moscas inequality, the Quantum threat is real and needs immediate attention.

key_claims.claim: NIST-selected PQC algorithms will be crucial for ensuring confidentiality, integrity, and authenticity in the post-quantum era as quantum computing evolves.
key_claims.quote: As quantum computing continues to evolve, these standards will play a pivotal role in ensuring the conﬁdentiality, integrity, and authenticity of digital communications in the post-quantum era [ 39].

key_claims.claim: QKD faces practical challenges including specialized hardware requirements, distance limitations due to photon loss, and noise-induced errors.
key_claims.quote:
Challenges with QKD are :
1. Practical Challenges: Requires specialized hardware (single-photon sources, quantum detectors).
2. Distance Limitations: Current implementations face limitations due to photon loss in optical ﬁbers over long distances.
3. Noisy Channels: Noise can introduce errors even in secure channels.

key_claims.claim: Protocols designed for quantum-resistant environments can enhance fairness in exchange, minimize delays, and provide robust authentication.
key_claims.quote:
Several simulation outcomes establish that the protocol enhances the 
fairness in exchange and minimize the delays and provide robust authentication [3].

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing can drastically speed up complex retail optimization tasks, reducing processing time from hours to seconds or minutes.
key_claims.quote: By part- nering with D-Wave Systems, the company optimized grocery inventory manage- ment, reducing task processing time from 25 h to just two minutes.

key_claims.claim: Quantum-enabled algorithms could uncover complex behavioral patterns and correlations that are masked by classical computational constraints.
key_claims.quote: Quantum computing offers a paradigm shift in predictive analytics, where quantum-enabled algorithms could uncover complex behavioral patterns and correlations that were previously masked by computational constraints [5].

key_claims.claim: Companies that integrate quantum solutions into operations may gain competitive advantage through improved efficiency and decision quality.
key_claims.quote: From a strategic perspective, the ability to harness quantum computing can become a source of competitive advantage and a cornerstone of innovation. Companies that successfully integrate quantum solutions into their operations may achieve leaps in operational efﬁciency and decision quality that competitors using classical analytics cannot easily match.

key_claims.claim: Current quantum computers are specialized and must be integrated in hybrid architectures with classical systems, making technology integration non-trivial.
key_claims.quote: Quantum computers today are specialized devices (often accessible via cloud services) that excel at certain tasks like optimization or probabilistic sampling but must work in concert with classical computers for data input/output and pre- or post-processing. This necessitates hybrid architectures and new IT integration strate- gies.
key_claims.location: Section 2.3 Technology Integration and Innovation / Page 257

key_claims.claim: Quantum-enhanced marketing could enable exhaustive data-driven decisions by evaluating combinatorially large numbers of scenarios at once.
key_claims.quote: In essence, quantum computing’s ability to consider a combinatorially large number of scenarios at once may allow marketers to move from intuition-driven or heuristics-driven decisions to truly exhaustive data-driven deci- sions.

key_claims.claim: Early corporate pilots in quantum computing are expected to yield first-mover advantages once the technology matures.
key_claims.quote: Analysts from McKinsey have observed that numerous companies are already conducting pilot experiments with quantum computing to build know-how, anticipating that those learnings will translate into ﬁrst-mover advantages once the technology matures [ 10].

key_claims.claim: Quantum-optimized inventory improved product availability and reduced stockouts, especially for high-demand items.
key_claims.quote: Store managers reported that product availability improved—shelves were replenished in a timelier manner, and instances of stockouts (products running out) were reduced, especially for high-demand items [9].
key_claims.location: Section 3.3 Impact on Inventory Management, Page 267-268

key_claims.claim: Quantum optimization likely balanced inventory to avoid overstocking and minimize waste in perishables.
key_claims.quote: Additionally, the optimization likely balanced inventory levels to avoid overstocking, which can lead to waste (especially in perishables).
key_claims.location: Section 3.3 Impact on Inventory Management, Page 268

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing enabled Save-On-Foods to tackle its most complex problems across the organization on an ongoing basis.
key_claims.quote: An ex ecutive noted that using quantum computing enabled them to attack their “most complex problems across the organization” on an ongoing basis, suggesting that the quantum approach was not a one-off trick but something that could continuously improve operations enterprise-wide [10].
key_claims.location: Section 3.3 Impact on Inventory Management, Page 268

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing’s capacity to analyze exponentially larger datasets enables mass personalization and individualized offers at scale.
key_claims.quote: Quantum computing’s capacity to analyze “exponentially larger datasets” and identify complex patterns means it could, for instance, compute optimal personalized offers for thousands of customers simultaneously [ 5].
key_claims.location: Section 3.4 Personalized Marketing and Loyalty Programs, Page 268-269

key_claims.claim: Volkswagen’s Quantum Shuttle pilot demonstrated that quantum computing can optimize consumer journeys in real time in a live deployment.
key_claims.quote: Importantly, this was the world’s ﬁrst known instance of a live quantum computing application directly affecting consumers in real time [13]. It was not just a lab simula- tion, people’s journeys were being optimized by a quantum processor on the ﬂy.

key_claims.claim: Quantum-routed buses experienced significantly reduced travel times and fewer delays compared to typical peak traffic conditions.
key_claims.quote: During the Web Summit week, these quantum-routed buses expe- rienced signiﬁcantly reduced travel times and fewer delays compared to what would be expected in typical peak trafﬁc conditions [ 15].

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing can coordinate routes for multiple vehicles simultaneously, unlike standard navigation apps that optimize each vehicle in isolation.
key_claims.quote: This approach is radically different from standard navigation apps that typically optimize one vehicle’s route in isolation. Instead, V olkswagen’s quantum system treated the ﬂeet of 9 buses as a coordinated whole, optimizing collectively to improve trafﬁc ﬂow for the group and, by extension, for all travelers on those roads.

key_claims.claim: Quantum annealing is effective for combinatorial optimization problems like inventory management and traffic routing, where classical methods are slow or suboptimal.
